q: Water standing upright without a pot.
My grandmother has a hundred children in one house; when they come out they are all wrapped in green.
My hut has a single pole and a roof of a thousand green feathers; I stand on the beach and drink the sea air.
hint: Its fruit gives oil and wine.

q: The more you take from me, the bigger I grow.
hint: What you dig in the ground.

q: I am a small black king; wherever I go my soldiers carry food for me and the land opens before me.
hint: A tiny insect that lives in colonies.

q: I am the mother of all streams, yet I am born in the sky and buried in the sea.
The old woman who wears a hundred skirts and cries when you undress her.
I speak every language but I have never been to school; I answer you from the cliff.
The chief's daughter who is beaten every day and still feeds the whole village.
Her husband is thin and tall; every morning he dances on her head while the women sing.
hint: The pole used to pound grain.

q: A white hen that lays its eggs in the grass; the eggs vanish when the sun looks for them.
hint: Water drops on grass at dawn.

q: I travel all over the country without legs and come back to the same village each night.
hint: Carries its house, leaves a silver trail.

q: I was born in water, I live in water, yet if I return to water I die.
The old man who never goes to the market, yet everyone brings him news.
hint: A forefather honoured by the family.

q: I wear a crown of thorns and a coat of armour, but inside I am sweet and gold.
hint: A tropical fruit with a spiky top.

q: A small dog that guards the house without barking and bites only the thief who touches it.
I run fast and leave no footprints; I knock down trees but no one has seen my face.
I carry my two eggs everywhere and never sit on them.
hint: A bull carries two of these on its head.

q: We are many brothers who sleep in one bed; when the eldest is pulled out, the rest catch fire.
hint: They live in a small box.

q: A man stands on one leg in the river all day; his clothes are grey and he catches what swims by.
Something you hold in your left hand but can never hold in your right.
I go into the forest a goat and come out a leopard.
hint: Plain cloth dyed into a spotted pattern.

q: Something that goes up the hill naked and comes down wearing a load of cloth.
My skin is a thousand eyes, my body is sweet, and my children are fighting inside a black blanket.
hint: Hot spice that makes you cough.

q: A thing I want badly but if I have it I lose it the moment I speak.
A little man who climbs the mountain each night and comes down when the cock crows.
I am a fire that does not burn, I appear after the storm and bow across the sky.
My hut is round, I have no door, I live under the sand and come out only after the first rains.
A king who has no kingdom and a crown that is red; he wakes the village without being asked.
hint: The cock that crows at dawn.

q: I am cut down and carried home, yet my children keep growing in my place.
hint: A root crop; new stems grow from cuttings.

q: A cow with a thousand spots who lies on the ground; the herdsman milks it with a cup of fire.
hint: A gourd used as a bowl.

q: The thing that walks with the dead and the living, has no name, and is paid by both.
I was born with teeth, I grow old with teeth, but I never eat.
I am given to you at birth, I grow only when you sleep, and the elders say I can be stolen by a sorcerer.
A big man sitting by the road; he gives water in the dry season and shade in the hot season.
hint: The great African tree of life.

q: A woman who gave birth to twins every season and buried them in the ground herself.
hint: Its tuber is planted to grow more.

q: I am the only one who can enter the king's house without bowing.
We are two who were born together, ate together and will be buried together, yet we never touched.
What travels from Cairo to Cape Town without moving at all?
A tall woman with long hair who sings when the wind passes and feeds the cattle.
